div.head: ECf 37.1
div.ab: Hoc autem dicebat, sepe se audisse in curia regis Francorum, dum ibi moratus esset; nec immerito: usura enim summa radix omnium uiciorum interpretatur.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 668 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

div.ab: And this he said he had often heard in the court of the king of the Franks, while he was staying there; and not undeservedly: for usury is interpreted as the chief root of all vices.

note.seg: Zur damaligen Beziehung des Französ. Königshauses zu den Herzögen der Normandie, aus der wohl dessen angebliches Ansehen in Eadwards Anschauung stammte: König Robert bezeugte am 13. Jan. 1024 eine Urk. zu Rouen neben dem Herzog (Pfister Rob. le Pieux p. lxxxi) und verlobte seine Tochter Richard dem III.

On the relation at that time of the French royal house to the dukes of Normandy, from which its alleged prestige in Edward's view probably derived: King Robert witnessed a charter at Rouen beside the duke on 13 Jan. 1024 (Pfister Rob. le Pieux p. lxxxi) and betrothed his daughter to Richard III
